title: The Evening Courier Newsroom
teaser: With an hour to go before the issue went to press, the editor locked himself in his office with the proofs of an exposé. When they broke the door down, the article was gone and nobody could help the editor any more. The print shop was waiting, and it ran a blank page.

habits.label: Purple lips
habits.habit: Lips stained by an indelible pencil
clues: A glass of water in the editor's office has a purple lip mark, the kind left by licking an indelible pencil. The culprit's lips are purple from an indelible pencil.
The margin of a surviving proof has a fresh correction in indelible pencil, its lead clearly licked. The culprit's lips are stained by an indelible pencil.

habits.label: Inky fingers
clues: The handle of a desk drawer in the office has black fingerprints in printer's ink. The culprit has printer's ink on their fingers.
There's a smudged black handprint on the door frame in reception, the same ink as in the composing room. The culprit has printer's ink on their fingers.

habits.label: Shorthand
clues: Shorthand squiggles have come off on the blotter on the editor's desk. The culprit knows shorthand.
In the smoking-room bin there's a scrap of notebook where a conversation with the editor is taken down in shorthand. The culprit writes shorthand.

habits.label: Sleeve guards
clues: A scrap of black sateen with a bit of elastic hangs on a nail by the office door frame. The culprit wears sateen sleeve guards.
The dusty office windowsill has two smooth elbow marks with shiny sateen fibres in them. The culprit wears sleeve guards.

habits.label: Tea through a sugar lump
habits.habit: Drinks tea through a lump of cracked sugar
clues: There are two glasses in metal holders on the editor's desk, one with crumbs of cracked sugar beside it, and Melnikov took his tea without sugar. The culprit sips tea through a sugar lump.
A lump of cracked sugar, bitten at the edge, lies on the floor by the office door. The culprit sips tea through a sugar lump.

habits.label: Smells of paste
clues: The office door handle is sticky with the flour paste used to stick up pages. The culprit smells of paste.
In the archive, last year's bound volume has sticky fingermarks that smell of paste. The culprit works with paste all day and smells of it.

habits.label: Scar over the brow
habits.habit: An eyebrow split by an old scar
clues: At 22:40 someone in the reporters' room saw a person in the corridor with an eyebrow split by a scar. The culprit has a scar over their brow.
The staff photo taken at 22:30 for the anniversary issue shows the edge of a face with a scar over the brow by the office door. The culprit has a scar over their brow.

habits.label: Felt hat
habits.habit: A grey felt hat with a wide band
clues: One hook on the coat stand in reception is empty, and a band torn from a grey felt hat lies on the office floor. The culprit wears a grey felt hat.
The baize on the editor's desk has a wet ring from a hat brim and grey felt fibres; it's raining outside. The culprit wears a felt hat.

habits.label: Dynamo fan
clues: The score of yesterday's Dynamo match is pencilled in the margin of a surviving proof, with "hurrah!" beside it. The culprit supports Dynamo.
There's a crumpled stand ticket for Sunday's game at the Dynamo stadium in the office waste basket. The culprit supports Dynamo.

habits.label: GTO badge
habits.habit: A GTO fitness badge on the lapel
clues: The clasp of a GTO fitness badge was found under the editor's chair. The culprit wears a GTO badge.
Through the glass door of reception someone saw a GTO badge glint on the lapel of the person leaving the office. The culprit wears a GTO badge.

habits.label: Dry cough
clues: At 22:35 someone in reception heard a dry, barking cough behind the office door, and Melnikov didn't have a cough. The culprit has a dry cough.
There's an empty chemist's bag from a herbal chest remedy in the office waste basket. The culprit has a dry cough.

habits.label: Writes epigrams
clues: On the back of a proof there's a fresh epigram about the editor in ink, with a perfect rhyme. The culprit writes epigrams.
An epigram about Melnikov is pinned to the board in the reporters' room, and at 22:30 the ink was still wet. The culprit writes epigrams.

habits.label: Odessa accent
clues: From the composing room someone heard a voice with an Odessa lilt by the office: "So what are you telling me, already?" The culprit has an Odessa accent.
The last entry in Melnikov's notebook: "22:30, talk about the article. Odessa accent, I'd know that voice." The culprit has an Odessa accent.

habits.label: Cracks sunflower seeds
clues: The ashtray on the editor's desk holds a little heap of sunflower seed husks. The culprit cracks sunflower seeds.
A trail of husks runs from the archive door to the office. The culprit cracks sunflower seeds.

habits.label: Galoshes
clues: There are wet diamond-patterned prints on the office parquet, the kind rubber galoshes leave. The culprit wears galoshes.
A single galosh with a red flannel lining was left on the archive doorstep. The culprit wears galoshes.

habits.label: Bandaged finger
habits.habit: An index finger in a bandage
clues: The office door handle has threads of gauze bandage and a drop of iodine on it. The culprit has a bandaged finger.
A surviving proof has a fingerprint where, instead of skin ridges, there's an even gauze mesh. The culprit has a bandaged finger.

late: A note set the meeting with the editor for "after midnight, as usual" before it was moved to 22:30. The culprit is a night owl.
The night-duty log has the same signature after two o'clock every single night. The culprit doesn't sleep at night.
french: A surviving proof has a note in French in the margin: "à supprimer". The culprit knows French.
Shortly before 22:45 a brief conversation in French was heard from the office. The culprit knows French.
glasses: A round lens from a pair of glasses lies on the office rug. The culprit wears glasses.
The baize on the desk has the imprint of a frame, as if glasses had been put down next to the proofs. The culprit wears glasses.
quiet: The reception parquet creaks under everyone, yet nobody there heard footsteps going to the office. The culprit moves silently.
The errand boys in the corridor didn't notice the office door open and close. The culprit moves silently.
tools: The office window latch was prised up with an awl and put back without a scratch. The culprit is handy with tools.
The desk drawer lock was taken apart and put back together with a screwdriver, every screw in place. The culprit is handy with tools.
strong: The office door was barred from the inside with a heavy fireproof cabinet, pushed a whole metre. The culprit is physically strong.
The editor's body was sat back in his chair as if he were working. The culprit is physically strong.
tech: The office telephone was dead: its line had been disconnected at the junction box in the press room. The culprit knows their way around machinery.
The lights in the corridor by the office went out at 22:40 because a fuse was pulled from the board. The culprit knows their way around machinery.
keys: The office lock was opened with its own key, and there isn't a scratch on the keyhole. The culprit had keys.
The archive cabinet with the 1933 volumes was opened with a key, not forced. The culprit had keys.
safe: The fireproof cabinet in the office was opened without force, and the article's proofs aren't in it. The culprit knows the safe combination.
The dial on the reception safe has been reset to zero, and a folder of letters is missing. The culprit knows the safe combination.
whistle: Over the clatter of the machines in the composing room someone heard whistling in the corridor. The culprit whistles.
At about 22:40 someone in the smoking room was whistling the march from Jolly Fellows. The culprit whistles.
sched: It all happened an hour before the issue went to press, when the night editor goes down to the composing room and reception empties. The culprit knows the schedule.
The timing fell exactly between the watchman's round and the errand boy coming for the pages. The culprit knows the schedule.
cash: A week's fees are missing from the newsroom cash box, and the payroll has other people's signatures on it. The culprit had access to money.
The envelope of money for the article's source is missing from the editor's desk. The culprit had access to money.
passages: A narrow gap behind the shelves leads from the archive to the composing room, and there are fresh tracks in the dust. The culprit knows the service passages.
Nobody went past reception, but the office is connected to the press room by the dumbwaiter for proofs. The culprit knows the service passages.
perfume: The office reeks of heavy perfume, and Melnikov couldn't stand it. The culprit wears heavy perfume.
A surviving proof smells of thick, sweet perfume. The culprit wears heavy perfume.
